stem: A client was classified as low risk for postpartum hemorrhage on admission to labor and delivery. During labor, new clinical factors increase the client’s hemorrhage risk. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Reassess and update the hemorrhage risk category and adjust anticipatory preparedness and resource planning according to the facility’s protocol.
options.B: Keep the original admission risk category because postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment is completed only once.
options.C: Wait until excessive bleeding occurs before changing the risk classification because risk tools are intended to diagnose hemorrhage after it begins.
options.D: Discontinue ongoing maternal assessment once a standardized risk score has been documented.

rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance supports stratifying an individual’s postpartum hemorrhage risk and updating that risk as clinical circumstances change, with anticipatory planning for management. A standardized risk tool helps organize preparedness but does not replace ongoing nursing assessment or diagnose hemorrhage after it has already occurred. B incorrectly treats risk as static. C defeats the preventive purpose of risk stratification. D is unsafe because a risk score complements, rather than replaces, continuous clinical assessment.
educational_objective: Use postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment as a dynamic care-planning tool by updating risk when clinical factors change and adjusting preparedness before hemorrhage occurs.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
source_document_title: Postpartum Hemorrhage Practice Bulletin No. 183; Oxytocin Shortage Clinical FAQ
source_version_date: Practice Bulletin reaffirmed 2024 with July 2025 Clinical Practice Update; ACOG FAQ current source accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Postpartum Hemorrhage PB — includes antenatal/intrapartum risk factors and an example risk-assessment tool within standardized hemorrhage bundles. ACOG Oxytocin Shortage FAQ, Intrapartum — ‘Stratify and update individual risk for postpartum hemorrhage, with anticipatory planning for management,’ referring to PB 183 Table 2
source_claim_supported: Postpartum hemorrhage risk stratification should inform anticipatory planning and should be updated as clinical circumstances change; it does not replace ongoing assessment or serve only as a post-hemorrhage diagnostic tool.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; reassess risk, revise the plan of care, and anticipate resources as client status changes
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — dynamic postpartum hemorrhage risk stratification and preparedness
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source purpose-recall item into a dynamic reassessment scenario and removed unsupported specificity about universal type-and-cross requirements by risk category. The final version uses ACOG’s direct recommendation to stratify and update hemorrhage risk with anticipatory planning. Category corrected from infection control to Management of Care.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: postpartum hemorrhage / dynamic risk assessment / preparedness
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against ACOG PB 183 and the ACOG clinical FAQ that explicitly instructs clinicians to stratify and update individual postpartum hemorrhage risk with anticipatory management planning.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A states only the supported reassessment and preparedness actions and leaves specific blood-bank testing/resources to the facility protocol and client risk. No universal risk-score thresholds are invented.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; changing risk factors require updated stratification and planning.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; ACOG explicitly supports updating risk rather than treating admission status as permanent.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; risk assessment is anticipatory and should occur before overt hemorrhage.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; standardized tools do not replace ongoing maternal assessment.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A uses the risk tool dynamically and integrates it into the evolving care plan.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address how the nurse should use the same standardized risk assessment over time.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is the best fit because the construct is ongoing risk reassessment and revision of resource planning.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked ACOG update-language, admission versus ongoing reassessment, prevention-versus-diagnosis distinction, resource-planning scope, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
